items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: Mike and Johnny and several other white boys I knew went to that school.

ctx.x: you got something outside. You got a stick. Did you say this was colored and white? Colored and white one day, yes. Wasn't that, wouldn't that be very unusual at that time?

Well, no, it wasn't unusual because I went to public school and I had a white teacher. I had a white teacher and I remember her name, put his own name of mine. My name was Mrs. O'Hallett. That's a big, it's a big, uh, high school back there, on Governor Nicklaus between Durban and Roman. I think it's Clark. I went there, it was called Byros. Oh, she was teaching us. That was unusual. But this man, when I was going to his school, uh, it was a little unusual, you know, but I know a lot of, uh, Italian people went…
He was, Professor Nelson, he was colored. He was colored. Professor, Medar,
